title: Feature flags + rollout config for incident bot collectors (per-channel, per-service)
author: Jacob Stein
release_notes:
- Adds rollout configuration for incident bot collectors (channel allowlist, per-service toggles, restricted-mode routing).
- Defaults remain OFF for all channels/services; must be explicitly enabled per rollout plan.
- Adds validation + safe defaults to avoid thread spam and accidental posting in sensitive incidents.
description:
Context
We’re starting phased enablement of the new collector-based context bundles. We need rollout controls that are (a) easy for on-call/SRE to operate during a shift, (b) safe by default (no accidental posting), and (c) flexible enough to do limited opt-ins (single rotation, single channel, single service).

This PR adds a dedicated rollout configuration layer + feature flags used by the Slack posting path and by the bundle assembly path.

What’s in this PR
- Rollout config model + loader
  - Introduces a single source of truth config file (YAML) for incident-bot rollout controls.
  - Supports runtime reload (polling) with jitter + backoff; last-known-good is kept on parse/validation failures.
- Controls
  - Per-channel allowlist: only post into explicitly listed Slack channels (e.g. #incidents, #incidents-bot-beta).
  - Per-service toggles: enable collectors by service (gateway, router, embeddings, etc.) and optionally by region.
  - Global kill switch: disable all posting without redeploy.
  - Restricted-mode routing:
    - If incident is marked sensitive/restricted (or matches configured criteria), bot posts a minimal stub to #incidents and full context bundle to a restricted channel.
    - Restricted channels must be explicitly allowlisted.
  - Rate-limit settings are plumbed here as well (thread spam control, requested in INT-1188).
- Surfacing
  - Adds “why not posted” debug breadcrumbs in logs (channel not allowlisted / service disabled / kill switch).
  - Adds a /incident-bot status command to print effective rollout state (no customer data, config only).

Config schema (YAML)
Example:
rollout:
  enabled: false
  allowed_channels:
    - C0123INCIDENTS   # #incidents
    - C0456BOTBETA     # #incidents-bot-beta
  restricted:
    enabled: true
    restricted_channels:
      - C0789INCIDENTS_RESTRICTED
  services:
    gateway:
      enabled: true
      regions: ["us-east", "us-west"]
      collectors:
        deploy: true
        config_diff: false
        saturation: false
    router:
      enabled: false
  limits:
    max_posts_per_incident_per_5m: 3
    collector_timeout_ms: 1800

Notes
- Defaults are safe: rollout.enabled=false, empty allowlist => bot will not post.
- If config is invalid, bot continues with last-known-good (and logs a metric + error).

Rollout plan checklist (Phase 1)
- [ ] Land config file with rollout.enabled=false in main.
- [ ] Create #incidents-bot-beta channel + get SRE + security approval for membership.
- [ ] Add channel IDs to allowed_channels; keep #incidents OFF initially.
- [ ] Enable for 1 rotation (SRE primary) + 2 services (gateway + control-plane) in us-east only.
- [ ] Monitor bot health metrics: post_success_rate, bundle_latency_p95, collector_error_rate by collector.
- [ ] Gather responder feedback in #eng-oncall (formatting, relevance, noise).
- [ ] Expand allowlist to #incidents after 1 week if noise <= target and no security regressions.
- [ ] Enable restricted-mode routing and confirm the restricted channel is configured before broad rollout.
- [ ] Add “kill switch” runbook entry for SRE (toggle rollout.enabled=false).

Testing
- Unit tests for config parsing/validation and defaulting.
- Integration test covers: allowlist denies posting, service toggles gate collectors, restricted-mode routes to restricted channel.

Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- UI in Console for viewing rollout state (PM-612 discussion).
- Auditing of config changes (security request; will be part of ENG-2847 workstream).

Screenshots / output
Example /incident-bot status:
rollout.enabled=false
allowed_channels=[C0456BOTBETA]
restricted.enabled=true restricted_channels=[C0789INCIDENTS_RESTRICTED]
services.gateway.enabled=true collectors={deploy:true, config_diff:false, saturation:false}

Risk
Low. Changes are config-gated and default OFF. Primary risk is misconfiguration; mitigated by strict validation + last-known-good.

slack: gate posting on channel allowlist + global kill switch
collectors: per-service/per-region enablement + wiring into bundle builder
restricted-mode: route full bundles to restricted channel; post stub to public thread

conversation:
Rafael Mendes (review): Can we make sure this is safe-by-default? I don’t want any path where a new deploy suddenly starts posting to #incidents.

Jacob Stein (author): Yep — rollout.enabled defaults false and allowed_channels defaults empty. Posting gate checks both before doing anything. Also added explicit log lines + metric with the deny reason.

Sean Gallagher (review): The checklist is great. One request: the kill switch should be operable without a redeploy.

Jacob Stein (author): Done — rollout.enabled is read from the config file and reloads every 30s (with jitter). Last-known-good is kept if a bad config is pushed.

Marcus Lin (security review): Restricted-mode behavior needs to guarantee that sensitive incidents never get full bundles posted to public channels. What’s the definition of “restricted” here?

Jacob Stein (author): In this PR it’s pluggable: we detect restricted mode based on incident metadata from the pager payload (is_restricted=true) OR a configured channel mapping (channel_id in restricted_channel_map). If restricted.enabled=true and we can’t resolve a restricted target channel, we fail closed (post nothing) and emit a metric.

Marcus Lin (security): Please add that fail-closed behavior explicitly and document it.

Jacob Stein (author): Added: if restricted.enabled and incident is restricted but restricted channel is missing, posting_gate denies all posting and surfaces ‘restricted_missing_target’. Also updated configs/rollout.example.yaml with comments.

Marissa Cole (product): For readability: can /incident-bot status avoid printing collector-level settings if it’s too noisy?

Jacob Stein (author): It prints a compact single-line summary by default; collector details are behind an optional “--verbose” argument.

Aisha Bello (SLOs): Any new metrics? Need to ensure we’re not adding high-cardinality labels.

Jacob Stein (author): Added counters for deny reasons with a small bounded enum label (reason=channel_not_allowed|rollout_disabled|service_disabled|restricted_missing_target). No incident IDs/channel names in labels.
